App.name: Field Signal
App.description: Help choosing a crop rotation, based on 25 years of satellite and weather data.

Footer.credit: Created at NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 · Data: NASA POWER, MODIS, SMAP, SoilGrids

Banner.title: Demo data
Banner.text: The numbers below are made up for this demo. Do not make decisions based on them.
Banner.offline: The server is not responding, so we are showing the data built into the app.

Common.errorTitle: We could not load the results
Common.errorText: The request was not accepted. Check what you entered and try again.

Field.title: About your field
Field.intro: Tell us where your field is and what you grow. We show how three rotations would have done over the last 25 years.
Field.whereHint: Drop a pin on the map, or draw the outline of your field.

draw.hint: Tap the map at each corner of your field, one after another. You need at least 3 corners.
draw.progress: {corners, plural, =0 {No corners yet} one {1 corner} other {# corners}} · {ha} ha
draw.tooSmall: The field is under {min} ha. Draw it larger: each hexagon is 1 ha.
draw.tooBig: The field is over {max} ha. Draw a single field.

Field.rotationHint: What you grow on this field, year after year. Between 2 and 4 crops.
Field.rotationFull: The rotation already has {max} years. Remove a crop to add another.
Field.prioritiesHint: Move the sliders. The further right, the more it matters.

yield.label: Reliable harvest
yield.hint: A harvest that stays steady from year to year

water.label: Water
water.hint: Crops that cope with dry summers

soil.label: Soil health
soil.hint: More organic matter, soil covered in winter

risk.label: Low risk
risk.hint: As few poor years as possible

Field.irrigatedHint: Turn on if you can water the crops in summer.

Results.loading: Analysing 25 years of data for this place…
Results.indicatorsTitle: What the data show for this place
Results.indicatorsHint: Latest year compared with the average of all years. The dashed line is the average.

carbon.label: Organic carbon
carbon.help: How rich the soil is in organic matter. More carbon usually means soil that holds water and nutrients better.

ph.label: pH
ph.help: How acidic or alkaline the soil is. Between 6 and 7.5 suits most field crops.

texture.label: Texture
texture.help: The mix of clay, sand and silt. Clay soils hold water longer; sandy soils dry out quickly.

Results.strategiesHint: The score shows how well each rotation fits your priorities. 100 is best.

strategy.rangeLabel: Likely score between {low} and {high}, most likely {mid}

Results.replayTitle: How each year would have gone
Results.replayHint: Each square is one season. Tap a square to see why.

replay.caption: Outcome of each rotation in each season
replay.noReasons: Nothing unusual in this season's data.

Results.explainHint: Pick a rotation to read the explanation.

generatedBy.template: Text built from a template, using only the values computed above.
generatedBy.llm: Text written by an AI model, using only the values computed above.

Results.planHint: Your field split into plots, one for each year of the rotation, so every crop in the plan is on the farm each year.

plan.tableCaption: Which crop each plot has in each season
plan.note: Example: {ha} ha of farmland split into {plots} plots. Each hexagon is exactly 1 ha. We left out hexagons on roads, buildings, water or woods, using OpenStreetMap. We drew the boundaries; they are not your field's. Crop heights on the map are exaggerated.
plan.noteDrawn: The field you drew is {area} ha. We cover it with {ha} farmable 1 ha hexagons, split into {plots} plots. We left out hexagons on roads, buildings, water or woods, using OpenStreetMap. Crop heights on the map are exaggerated.

Feed.title: Where to buy feed this year?
Feed.intro: For each commune: whether there will be enough harvest, what quality risks there are, and how kind to the environment the farming is.
Feed.mapHint: Colour and symbol show the risk of not finding enough harvest. Tap a commune for details.
Feed.noZones: We have no zones for this region yet.

zone.flagDays: {observed} risky days this year, versus {normal} in a normal year
zone.lowerRiskMaize: Rotations with soybean or sunflower usually lower this risk over 3 years. Compare them for a field in this commune.
zone.lowerRiskOther: Not growing the same crop two years in a row usually lowers this risk over 3 years. Compare rotations for a field in this commune.

Feed.compareHint: Pick two communes and see which is safer for the chosen crop: quantity, quality and water.

compare.summary: For {crop}, {a} is better on {winsA} of {total} measures, {b} on {winsB}.
compare.caption: {a} compared with {b}, for {crop}
compare.note: "Better" only compares these two zones, measure by measure. All numbers are estimates with a range; check each zone's confidence.

adoption.title: How much more {crop} the area could supply
adoption.hint: Move the slider: the share of suppliers who add the crop to their rotation.
adoption.linear: Results grow in proportion to the adoption share, starting from the scenario computed for {base}%.
adoption.peaArea: Feed pea: the same extra area as the soybean scenario (the same share of land changes crop).
adoption.peaYield: Feed pea yield: {low} to {high} t/ha, most likely {mid} t/ha. Placeholder value, to verify with an agronomist.
adoption.peaProtein: Feed pea protein as harvested: {low} to {high}% (crop table, low confidence). To verify with an agronomist.
adoption.bothSum: Both: the same extra area, half soybean and half feed pea. Harvest and protein are the sum of the two halves.
adoption.soyScenario: Soybean values come from the scenario computed by the model.

About.title: About Field Signal
About.intro: Field Signal brings together 25 years of data on weather, soil moisture and plant health, so you can see how different rotations would have done on your field.
About.judgment: The tool supports the farmer's judgment. It does not replace it.

what.farmer: For farmers: compares your current rotation with two alternatives (at least one with soybean or peas) and shows, year by year, how each would have done.
what.buyer: For feed buyers: shows, by commune, the risk of not finding enough harvest, quality risks (aflatoxins, fusarium, harvest rain) and environmental impact.
what.transparency: Every number shows its source, period, assumptions and confidence next to it.

About.sourcesHint: Public data. Resolution shows how big each source's “pixel” is.

sources.power: Heat, rain and air humidity, day by day
sources.modis: How green and vigorous the vegetation is (NDVI)
sources.smap: Water in the soil, around the roots
sources.soilgrids: Organic carbon, pH and soil texture
sources.eucropmap: Which crops grow where, for areas per commune
sources.ins: Official county yields, to check the model

ai.model: A small model estimates the chance of a poor year for each zone and crop, from weather and vegetation signals in the critical periods. We test it by leaving out one year at a time and publish both hits and misses.
ai.text: A language model turns the computed numbers into plain text. It may only use values we computed, in a fixed format.

limits.hail: Hail and other short, local weather events.
limits.pests: Pests and diseases in your field.
limits.management: Your field work, hybrids and fertiliser.
limits.scale: Weather data describe an area tens of kilometres wide, not your exact plot.

About.demo: In this version the numbers are for demonstration. We mark them clearly as “Demo data” until the real data are connected.
About.judgmentDetail: It shows what would have happened in past years. The decision for your field stays yours.
About.nasaNote: We use free public data published by NASA and other institutions. NASA is not a partner and does not endorse this tool.
About.aiHint: AI does two small, checkable jobs. It does not make decisions for you.

Simulator.title: See your rotation on a field
Simulator.intro: A small tractor sows each crop of the rotation, the field grows and is harvested, then the next crop follows. Brown means bare soil; green means the field is covered.
Simulator.banner: Illustration — not a machine work plan.
Simulator.demoNote: Demo rotations and a demo field near Aiud. Sowing and harvest months are typical for Alba county; yours will differ.
Simulator.noWebgl: 3D is not available on this device, so here is a flat view of the same field.

phase.harvestCover: Cover crop worked into the soil

controls.keys: Keys: Space play or pause · ← → step · 1 2 4 speed · R restart · C camera

stats.title: Field work, per operation
stats.illustrative: Illustrative estimates for this demo field, not a work plan.
stats.bare: Months of bare soil between crops

Simulator.seasonRowCover: sown in {sow}, worked into the soil in {harvest}
Simulator.reducedMotion: Reduced motion is on, so the field does not animate. Use Back and Next to step through each season.
